articles.title: Kumkum Mohod wins Asian Games gold, secures India’s 2028 Olympic quota
articles.summary: Teenager Kumkum Mohod kept her composure under pressure to clinch gold in the women’s individual recurve event at the Asian Games, defeating South Korea’s
articles.body: Teenager Kumkum Mohod kept her composure under pressure to clinch gold in the women’s individual recurve event at the Asian Games, defeating South Korea’s Oh Yejin in a shoot-out here on Saturday.With the victory, Kumkum became the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games medal in the individual recurve event.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal TallyAfter the scores were tied at 5-5, Kumkum held her nerve in the shoot-out, shooting a 10 while Oh managed an 8 to hand the Indian the gold medal.The victory capped a remarkable campaign for Kumkum, who had already secured an Olympic quota place for India by reaching the semifinals. She defeated China’s Jingyi Zhu 6-2 to book her place in the final and assure herself of at least a silver medal.Kumkum secured one of the two available quota places for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. As per the rules, the quota belongs to the country.Against Zhu, Kumkum won the opening set 28-27 after shooting 9, 10 and 9. The second set was shared after both archers shot three 10s, while the third set was also tied, leaving Kumkum with a 4-2 lead.She then edged Zhu by a point in the final set to seal a 6-2 victory, with the scores reading 28-27, 30-30, 29-29 and 29-28.Earlier in the day, Kumkum defeated reigning world champion Kang Chaeyoung 6-4 in the quarterfinal.The individual gold was her third medal at the Asian Games. Kumkum had earlier won the women’s team recurve gold alongside Ankita Bhakat and Kirti Sharma, before combining with Dhiraj Bommadevara to claim mixed pair silver on Friday.Kumkum’s gold also marked a landmark moment for Indian recurve archery, making her the first Indian woman to win a medal in the individual event at the Asian Games.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Indian kurash player Yash Kumar Chauhan provisionally suspended after failed dope test
articles.summary: Indian kurash player Yash Kumar Chauhan has been provisionally suspended after returning an adverse analytical finding for multiple banned substances from
articles.body: Indian kurash player Yash Kumar Chauhan has been provisionally suspended after returning an adverse analytical finding for multiple banned substances from a sample collected during the Asian Games on September 27, the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) announced on Saturday.The 24-year-old's sample, tested by the International Testing Agency (ITA) on behalf of the OCA, was found to contain metabolites of Metandienone and GW1516, along with Mephentermine and its metabolite.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal Tally"The ITA, on behalf of the OCA, reports that a sample collected from kurash athlete Yash Kumar Chauhan (IND) has returned an Adverse Analytical Finding for non-specified prohibited substances Metandienone metabolites, GW1516 metabolites, Mephentermine and its metabolite," the OCA said in a statement.Chauhan has been provisionally suspended with immediate effect pending the resolution of the case under the World Anti-Doping Code and OCA Anti-Doping Rules. The suspension prevents him from competing, training, coaching or participating in any activity during the Asian Games.Metandienone, an anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from testosterone, is prohibited at all times under the WADA Code. GW1516 is also prohibited at all times, while Mephentermine is a non-specified stimulant prohibited in competition.The OCA said Chauhan has the right to challenge the provisional suspension before the Court of Arbitration for Sport's Anti-Doping Division. He can also request analysis of his B-sample.The kurash competition at the Asian Games was held from September 26 to 29. Chauhan competed in the men's 90kg category and lost to Tajikistan's Mirmamadov Shakarmamad in the round of 16 on September 27, the day his sample was collected.India won one medal in kurash at the Games, with Pincky Balhara claiming bronze in the women's 78kg category.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Pranavi Urs scripts history, becomes first Indian woman golfer to win Asian Games gold
articles.summary: Pranavi Urs on Saturday became the first Indian woman golfer to win an individual gold medal at the Asian Games, holding on to a slender one-stroke lead
articles.body: Pranavi Urs on Saturday became the first Indian woman golfer to win an individual gold medal at the Asian Games, holding on to a slender one-stroke lead in the final round to create history and help India claim silver in the team event.The 23-year-old from Mysore recovered from a difficult start to the final round, making three birdies after a triple bogey on the third hole had wiped out her three-stroke overnight lead.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal TallyPranavi carded an even-par 70 in the final round to finish with a four-day total of 15-under 265, one stroke clear of the chasing pack.Her performance also proved crucial to India's team silver, with Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar joining her in the women's team event. Aditi shot 67 in the final round, while Diksha carded 77.The two best scores from the three-member team count towards the team medal, with India finishing at 14-under 546. China won gold with a total of 22-under 538.Pranavi's individual gold was India's first in Asian Games golf since Shiv Kapur won the men's individual title in 2002. She is now the first Indian woman to claim the top prize in the individual golf event at the continental Games.Earlier, Teenager Kumkum Mohod kept her composure under pressure to clinch gold in the women’s individual recurve event at the Asian Games, defeating South Korea’s Oh Yejin in a shoot-out here on Saturday.With the victory, Kumkum became the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games medal in the individual recurve event.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Northwestern Wildcats christen new Ryan Field with impressive win over Penn State Nittany Lions
articles.summary: Northwestern christened the new $875 million Ryan Field with a dominant 34-13 win over Penn State, racking up 413 rushing yards in the Big Ten clash.
articles.body: After spending some time playing in a (very cool) makeshift stadium on the shores of Lake Michigan, the Northwestern Wildcats finally christened the new Ryan Field in an important Big Ten clash with Penn State. Both teams came in with one loss, and another would almost certainly tank any hopes of getting into the Big Ten Championship conversation. The Wildcats came in off of an impressive showing against Indiana, and it became evident that that was no fluke, thanks to a 34-13 win over the Nittany Lions. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE But before the game, Northwestern took a second to show off their new $875 million home — which opened its doors 100 years to the day after its predecessor debuted — and it was spectacular. The first points at the new Ryan Field went to — fittingly enough — the Wildcats when Jackson Kleather booted a 50-yarder between the uprights to cap off Northwestern's maiden drive in their new home. The Nittany Lions were forced to punt on their opening drive, and OC Chip Kelly's Wildcats offense went right back to work. Running back Joseph Himon II threw down a massive 47-yard run to put the Wildcats on the Penn State 4-yard line. Two plays later, quarterback Aidan Chiles used his legs to power into the end zone for six. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER The Wildcats couldn't have asked for a better opening quarter with 144 yards of total offense, 109 of those coming on the ground. However, in the second quarter, Penn State forced a fumble on the Wildcats' second drive and recovered, giving them prime field position. That eventually led to an 8-yard rushing touchdown for running back Carson Hansen. Northwestern struck right back with a quick touchdown on the ensuing possession, which stood after a flag for a block in the back was picked up. Northwestern tacked on another touchdown to go up 24-7. On their final drive of the half, Penn State looked like they were going to at least put three points on the board; however, kicker Ryan Barker — who was staring down the barrel of Northwestern's new, European soccer-style "Wildcat Wall" — missed a crucial 45-yard field goal attempt. David Braun's Wildcats dominated in that first half with 278 yards of offense. That trend continued in the second half. The Nittany Lions continued to struggle to get anything going offensively, while on defense, they couldn't find a way to contain the Wildcats' running game. If you thought it couldn't get worse for Penn State, it did. On the first play of the fourth quarter, Nittany Lions quarterback Rocco Becht threw an interception at midfield, leaving a possible scoring opportunity on the table. While Penn State was able to put some points on the board, there was never a doubt that the Wildcats were in control. While the 34-13 final is enough to get the Wildcats some attention, the fact that they put up 506 yards of total offense, 413 of them on the ground, is going to make defensive coordinators a bit nervous moving forward. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Penn State will head home to host USC next weekend, while Northwestern will spend another week at their new digs and will welcome Ball State.

articles.title: No-handshake policy continues as Shreyas Iyer, Sahibzada Farhan skip customary greeting at Asian Games final
articles.summary: Indian skipper Shreyas Iyer and Pakistan captain Sahibzada Farhan did not shake hands at the toss ahead of the men's cricket final at the Asian Games in
articles.body: Indian skipper Shreyas Iyer and Pakistan captain Sahibzada Farhan did not shake hands at the toss ahead of the men's cricket final at the Asian Games in Japan on Saturday, continuing the no-handshake practice seen between the two teams since last year's Asia Cup.The two captains came out for the toss before the gold-medal clash, but live visuals showed no handshake between Iyer and Farhan. India won the toss and elected to bat.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal TallyIndia have also retained the same XI that featured in their previous match, with 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi continuing at the top of the order alongside Abhishek Sharma.The no-handshake practice has continued since the Asia Cup in September last year. It comes against the backdrop of cross-border tensions and military developments between India and Pakistan, including Operation Sindoor.Since then, Indian cricket teams have followed a no-handshake approach in recent fixtures against Pakistan in ICC and ACC tournaments.Saturday's final is the first men's cricket meeting between India and Pakistan at the Asian Games, with the gold medal at stake in Nisshin.The Indian women's cricket team also won gold at the Asian Games by defeating Sri Lanka in the final.Teams:Pakistan (Playing XI): Sahibzada Farhan(c), Maaz Sadaqat, Usman Khan(w), Saim Ayub, Hasan Nawaz, Abdul Samad, Arafat Minhas, Ahmed Daniyal, Saad Masood, Abrar Ahmed, Sufyan MoqimIndia (Playing XI): Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson(w), Shreyas Iyer(c), Ishan Kishan, Tilak Varma, Shivam Dube, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Ravi Bishnoi, Jasprit BumrahStay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Seneca tops Monett in high-scoring affair
articles.summary: Seneca came out on top against Monett in a matchup that featured 90 combined points! See our recap and highlights below from the Indians' third-straight win.
articles.body:
SENECA, MO. — Seneca High School Football has now rattled off three consecutive wins following a 1-2 start, taking down Monett 52-38 at home on Friday.

The Indians came out of the gates firing. Seneca opened things up with a 22-0 scoring run before the Monett offense got things going.

While Seneca deploys a run-first approach, Monett has one of the top passing attacks in the Show-Me State. That passing game got going later in the contest, including a pair of TDs through the air from Dylan Washick, one to Brayden Seitz and another to Carson Nestleroad in the first half.

However whether it be Klay Davidson, Silas Ball or Brailen Hicks, the Cubs had no answer to slow down the Seneca run game.

With the win, Seneca moves to 4-2 overall while Monett drops to 3-3. Both squads will be back in action next week with Seneca facing Aurora on Thursday, October 8 and Monett hosting McDonald County on Friday, October 9.

articles.body:
England will look to build on a strong win in the Czech Republic as they face another tricky away trip in Croatia .

Thomas Tuchel's side bounced back from a defeat to Spain in their Nations League opener as they produced a professional performance against 10-man opposition on Tuesday.

That 2-0 success leaves them second in Group A3, level on points with their opposition – who will not benefit from their usual home advantage due to crowd restrictions in Rijeka.

Croatia were beaten 4-2 by England at the World Cup and are now back under the management of former West Ham boss Slaven Bilic, who previously oversaw the national team between 2006 and 2012.

Croatia vs England is due to kick off at 5pm BST on Saturday 3 October at the HNK Rijeka Stadium.

Viewers in the United Kingdom can watch the match live on ITV1, with coverage from 4.15pm BSt. A live stream will be available via ITVX.

Martin Erlic has withdrawn from the Croatia squad after suffering a hamstring strain.

Manchester City's Nico O'Reilly withdrew from the England squad earlier this week, leaving Lewis Hall likely to continue at left-back. Trent Alexander-Arnold impressed with an assist against the Czech Republic and will contend for a place again on the right of the back four, while Jordan Pickford will displace James Trafford in goal. Alex Scott could earn a first start.

Croatia XI : Livakovic; Smolcic, Vuskovic, Gvardiol, Perisic; Modric, Kovacic P. Sucic; Baturina, Beljo, Marco Pasalic

England XI : Pickford; Alexander-Arnold, Konsa, Guehi, Hall; Anderson, Scott; Rogers, Bellingham, Gordon; Kane.

articles.title: On his 57th and final homecoming, Dwight Lundeen's 'Dogs rout Tech 57-0
articles.summary: "This homecoming ranks number one." Head coach Dwight Lundeen honored accordingly as Becker routs Tech 57-0 in homecoming win.
articles.body:
BECKER — With 5:07 left in the third quarter, Becker football senior Tarver Schendzielos fielded a free kick off a couple of bounces and proceeded to weave his way through the Tech coverage to go up 57-0 over the Tigers.

Then the offense rushed out onto the field to take a knee on the extra point; their work had been done. A big "57" on the scoreboard luminated the field at Dwight Lundeen Stadium as the legendary coach the stadium is named after sulked up his final homecoming win, in his 57th season, adding to career total of over 400 wins.

"[This homecoming] probably ranks number one," Lundeen said. "It was very unique the way we ended up with that, and then the whole team thought, 'No matter what, we're not going to score.' That was special. It's fitting to have your last homecoming game ever end on 57 points. I'm really proud of the kids; they're a wonderful group."

It was not just the 2026 team honoring the school's first and only head coach. It was 57 years' worth of former players and coaches congregated back to their old stomping grounds to celebrate the legendary coach.

"That was amazing," Lundeen said. "I couldn't stop crying."

The night was a synopsis of six decades of Becker football under Lundeen: four state championships, hundreds of players and a yearly varsity squad that united an entire community together year-after-year.

Scoring as many points as they did and winning in shutout fashion was simply the cherry on top.

"It was awesome to look at the scoreboard, and it said 57," Schendzielos said. "To know it was 57 years of coach Dwight; that just meant something. To see my coach crying was special, it really meant something to him and that was the best part. If he needed something from me, I jump in a matter of seconds, no matter what it is. He's made me a better man throughout the year; I just love him."

Since starting the year 0-3, the Bulldogs have since scored 111 points over the last two weeks and are finally playing with the confidence that they entered the season with.

Senior quarterback Tristan Kowalkowski does not take lightly the role he plays in the history of Becker football as the final starting quarterback under Lundeen.

"It was special seeing because we worked really hard for this," Kowalkowski said. "Emotions were high, and it was just a special night with everybody here and celebrating the same thing. You see all the generations and all the people that he's worked with, and all of the hard work that he's put in with every single player. Being a part of that 57 is something special."

Just a couple of years removed from an undefeated state title run in 2024, the Bulldogs know what it takes to make a run back to US Bank Stadium. Kowalkowski started that season as a sophomore and linebacker Cody Deters had five sacks and 40 tackles anchoring the defense. Chase Stupar and Bennett Kujawa each contributed as well.

The D.N.A from that championship roster is still alive and well on this Becker squad, now they are seniors committed to get back to The Bank.

"We're going to be a really tough out right now," Lundeen said. "We work really, really hard on Monday's and fix what we can fix and then keep them positive. It has worked out well; we're playing pretty good football."

Becker is home against Totino-Grace next week on Oct. 9 before its season ends on the road against Rocori on Oct. 14 and Detroit Lakes on Oct. 21.

"I don't think anybody can break our confidence right now," Kowalkowski said. "We're high, and we're going to keep that going into the next game. We're going to carry this into TG, and we're going to win."

articles.title: Week 7 Roundup: Melbourne takes down Viera for first time since 2022
articles.summary: For the first time since 2022, Melbourne defeated Viera with a wire-to-wire 42-13 win to pick up its first district win of the season.
articles.body:
MELBOURNE — Coming off a bye week, Melbourne High was eagerly awaiting its district showdown with Viera on Oct. 2. The Hawks entered the meeting on a three-game winning streak over the Bulldogs.

For this Melbourne senior class, they got a taste of victory over Viera for the first time as the Bulldogs set the tone from the opening kickoff to blow out the Hawks 42-13.

"We're incredibly proud. It's been like a monkey on our back we've been trying to get off. Viera has had our number. It's no secret," Melbourne head coach Jeff Pannucci said. "We just can't seem to find a way to get over the hump, but these seniors had never beaten Viera and that was their goal. It feels real good when they set out a goal and they accomplish it. I'm happy for the seniors, I'm happy for the football team and I'm happy for Melbourne High."

Melbourne dominates Viera in district football 42-13

With Viera scheming to contain Melbourne sophomore tailback Tyrese Jefferson, it was the big passing plays from junior quarterback Will Reinhold that was the difference.

Reinhold finished the night completing 5-of-8 passes for 141 yards and 3 touchdowns.

"It feels amazing. We haven't beaten Viera in a minute," Reinhold said. "We put in that score against them from the first play."

The junior lobbed a 42-yard touchdown pass to Jefferson to increase the Melbourne lead to 21-0. On the next possession, Reinhold hit senior Jeremiah Thomas for a 20-yard touchdown on 3rd-and-8. His final touchdown pass with a 65-yard play-action pass to senior DJ Scott with 45 seconds remaining in the first half.

"The offense totally executed that whole entire game," Reinhold said. "Just executing from start to finish every single play. Made smart choices."

Reinhold recorded his first game with multiple touchdown passes. The junior entered the game with 4 touchdowns in four starts. After recording zero varsity starts before this season, Reinhold is closing in on the 1,000-yard mark.

"This is the first time he's started varsity games, so it just takes time. You can see he's getting more and more comfortable. He's winning games with his arm, which we needed when you got a guy like Tyrese (Jefferson) and they're going to send eight or nine guys at him. You got to be able to do that," Pannucci said. "He's growing as a quarterback. He's an incredible leader. Extremely proud of him. He always did the right things when he was not the starting quarterback. He never wavered and it's hard to find kids like that."

The junior said his confidence has increased each game. In his previous two starts, Reinhold threw for over 200 yards on double-digit completions.

"I've seen (my growth) expand exponentially," Reinhold said. "From the first week to now, I feel so much more comfortable and it's an amazing feeling."

Melbourne opened the scoring 13 seconds into the game on a 98-yard kick return for a touchdown by senior Howard Dewitt. It was the senior's third special teams touchdown this season.

"Our kickoffs all night were pinning them deep and they were having problems with that," Pannucci said. "When you return a kick for a touchdown, that's a backbreaker. Special teams were our focus because it hurt us in the Oviedo game and we did a good job fixing that."

That score jolted Melbourne into controlling the rest of the game. Jefferson finished the night with a pair of rushing touchdowns of 8 and 9 yards. The defense limited Viera to 13 first downs and 2 rushing touchdowns.

Bulldogs sophomore TJ Ross and junior Silas Walters sacked Viera quarterback Jaamal Crittington. Melbourne sophomore Aaron Pierce tipped a ball in the air and intercepted a pass to set up Melbourne's final touchdown of the night.

"We did a fantastic job. All week we prepped the same way. We created turnovers, we made stops in the backfield, created negative plays," Pannucci said. "It was exactly what the game plan was. We were going to live with certain things underneath and they executed the game plan perfectly."

Melbourne picked up its first district win of the season and moved to 4-2. The Bulldogs look to carry momentum into another district game on Oct. 9 versus Lake Howell.

"I told them to enjoy it. Lake Howell is a really good football team, so we're going to have to lock in and find a way to be a really good football team," Pannucci said. "Monday's going to come around and this is no longer going to feel good anymore. We're going to find a way to lock in on Lake Howell."

Viera fell behind early and couldn't change the momentum as the Hawks allowed the first 21 points of the game and trailed 35-7 at halftime.

"We had to figure out where we were as a team," Viera head coach Tony Gulla said. "We just got behind early with special teams. Can't make mistakes like that against good teams."

The Hawks' special teams struggled early, allowing the kick return for a touchdown and several short punts that resulted in Melbourne having short fields. Melbourne recorded an average starting field position of its own 44-yard line.

"It was big difference. It was 14-0 before you blinked. We're not a real passing team, so we're behind the 8-ball. Got to give credit to Melbourne and the staff," Gulla said. "They've been planning for this game for a year. I know they have and they did a real good job shutting us down and taking advantage of our weaknesses."

A bright spot for the Viera offense was the full return of senior tailback Duke Butler. In his fourth game of the season, Butler ended the night with 9 rushes for 73 yards and 2 touchdowns.

"The one good thing we found out is that (Butler's) 100%. Last week, he tried to play and didn't feel right," Gulla said. "Everyone's been telling me you got to get through the pain and obviously he got through the pain. In a close game, I think we would have been able to rely on him."

Viera did its job limiting Jefferson on the ground. The Melbourne tailback finished with a season-low 36 rushing yards on 13 carries. However, it was the big passing plays that cost Viera.

"We did a good job with that. That was the emphasis of the week, but you got to cover people. They were smart," Gulla said. "They realized we were shutting the running game down and they were going to pass and they did a good job."

Viera drops to 1-1 in district play and 3-3 overall. The Hawks host Oviedo in another district matchup on Oct. 9

"We beat Oviedo next week and we're right back in it," Gulla said. "We got Lake Howell and Oviedo to get back in it. We got to regroup though. We got to do a better job coaching."

articles.title: 3 Stars: Slow start, clicking skates, & Hintz is okay in loss vs Blues
articles.summary: The Dallas Stars started slow and couldn’t beat Joel Hofer in a 4-0 loss against the St. Louis Blues at American Airlines Center on Friday. Stars lines Scrat...
articles.body:
The Dallas Stars started slow and couldn't beat Joel Hofer in a 4-0 loss against the St. Louis Blues at American Airlines Center on Friday.

Scratches: Blackwell, Capobianco, Duchene (injured)

It's the first game of the season, but EW

The first period of the season was ugly, especially for Dallas.

St. Louis did an excellent job exploiting the Stars in their own end. When Dallas tried to push the puck up the wall, the Blues pinched and closed it off. When they tried to move it up the middle, St. Louis locked it down. And when they tried to hit the long stretch pass, it wasn't available.

Then there were mistakes like Thomas Harley trying a pass through a forechecker in the middle of the slot. That's not tactics, that's just poor decision-making. Hoping that isn't a theme here for Harley.

As Glen Gulutzan said this morning, Blues coach Jim Montgomery is such a smart tactician behind the bench. He knows the Stars system well and adjusts accordingly. Gulutzan said he was taking notes on Montgomery's adjustments during the preseason.

So far, Monty has the leg up after one period. Let's see how Gulutzan can respond.

Once the Blues took back control of the puck in the Dallas end, they didn't so much attack right away or even cycle. Instead, we saw a lot of stopping, setting up in an umbrella, and looking for direct passes. With the Stars crashing down to the posts and matching up with forwards around Jake Oettinger, the trailing forward or defenseman was open a few times on the backside with passes through the slot.

The only goal of the period came off an unlucky Robertson shot hitting Harley in the back of the leg and some miscommunication and poor handling of an odd-man rush by Dallas. Neither Rantanen nor Wyatt Johnston located the Blues on the backside, and a bouncing puck eventually found its way in off the stick of Mason McTavish.

"Just got to start playing a simple game, not try to go East and West at the blue line," Hintz said of how to overcome slow starts. "Try to just get pucks to the net and try to hold the puck a little bit longer in the O-zone… Starts with little things."

Offensively, Dallas created a few nice chances.

Jason Robertson nearly surprised Blues goalie Joel Hofer with a short-side shot off the rush on the power play. Hofer barely recovered after his sweeping bank pass behind his own net came back out to Joel Kiviranta on the back post. Roope Hintz missed high after a nice pass by Mikko Rantanen from behind the net. And Tyler Seguin (YES, he's back) had a nice redirection in the slot, once again set up by Rantanen on the power play.

The Stars kept Rantanen out for both power-play units, but replaced the other four skaters. I imagine that Robertson will also stay out there when he has the energy, meaning PP2 will be Harley, Robertson, Rantanen, Benn, and Seguin.

That's two good units with varying tactics. PP1 moving the puck around more and attacking from the walls, while PP2 is likely to get shots through from the point and allow Benn and Seguin to tip and pick up rebounds. Tough to defend. No reason this PP shouldn't be top five in the league again this year.

Well, the adjustments worked. Dallas looked so much better in period two.

The Stars came out fast, put far more pressure on the Blues, and created some good chances. Really, it was a complete role reversal from the first. St. Louis struggled to get control of the puck, Hofer was adventurous as ever out of his crease, and the Stars looked more in control all over the ice.

Unfortunately, it was the Blues who once again scored the only goal of the period. But really, it was all Dallas that led to it.

Oettinger came out to play a puck rimmed behind his net, but had a funky in-between handoff with Nils Lundkvist that allowed St. Louis to get a stick in and gain control in the left circle. Just as that happened, Hintz came sweeping through the top of the crease and clicked his skates with Oettinger, who was facing the other direction.

Oettinger took a tumble and ended up lying down well out of position. Dalibor Dvorsky took advantage and cashed in on the wide-open net while Oettinger looked like when you accidentally take control of the goalie in an NHL video game and immediately stack the pads and hit all the buttons.

Oof. 2-0 Blues despite a solid period for Dallas and not much offensively for St. Louis.

A fun little moment in the period came when Arttu Hyry hit Jake Neighbours into the boards from behind, which I cannot believe wasn't called a penalty. Probably could've even been a major.

After Hyry shook off Jimmy Snuggerud's half-assed attempt of a scrum, he was jumped by Neighbours and sort of fought. Hyry did not look comfortable, Neighbours maybe landed one punch while Hyry was on his knees, and Dallas got a power play out of it.

Hyry already had some sort of bandage on his chin early in the game and had blood on his chin and sweater after the tilt. I can imagine the Blues were not happy about the no-call on the boarding hit AND the extra minor to go with it.

Remember, while it is important to win games early in the season, the priority is to get your game together and shake off the rust, especially for Dallas after a loooooong summer. They got much better after the first period and still have 20 minutes to find two or more goals and get something out of the season opener.

Hintz was injured and down on the ice after a knee-on-knee collision with Brandon Carlo. Carlo was attacked by Harley and given a major penalty and game misconduct. It looked scary, but Hintz was back on the Dallas bench soon after.

"Feeling fine," Hintz said after the game. "I think I got a little lucky there. At first I thought something happened really bad. But I got back there pretty quick."

"Not great to see. It's a dirty hit, and you don't want to see that happen," Miro Heiskanen said. "Hopefully, he's good and not bigger issues or anything. But it was great to see him back pretty quickly after that."

Unfortunately, Harley was given a minor for cross-checking, the Stars power play created nothing once they got through the 4-on-4, and Tyler Seguin took a double minor for high-sticking that flipped the momentum completely.

This game was wacky. Multiple injured players for the Blues, one for Dallas (Hintz), a fight (kinda), funky goals, one of which was reversed, and some overall sloppiness. First game of the season, alright.

"I thought that they got to their game quicker than we did. We were a little sloppy, kind of fed their attack. Then when they got the goal, it was a little bit of a bounce there that they got. Two of our players collided, and that gave them energy, and we kept feeding it a little bit. At the end of the day, they got to their game quicker than we did, and they stayed with it the whole way. We need to be a little bit sharper, certainly in our start."

Dylan Hryckowian tied the game for Texas with 21 seconds left, and the Stars beat the Iowa Wild in the shootout.

This game had quite a bit of "first-game-of-the-season-itis" for both teams.

The crowd was AWESOME, as expected, for the season and home opener. I especially loved the ovation for Gulutzan and Seguin during player intros.

articles.title: Virginia Tech football: 6 takeaways from Hokies’ heartbreaking loss to Pitt
articles.summary: A lot to talk about. Here are six takeaways.
articles.body:
The Virginia Tech Hokies lost their first game of the James Franklin era on Friday night, falling 35-33 to the Pittsburgh Panthers. However, that result isn't without some controversy — more on that later.

Virginia Tech outgained Pittsburgh 499 to 295 and still lost. Those weren't junk yards either. The Hokies dominated until self-inflicted mistakes gave Pitt the ball in tremendous field position. For the most part, the Panthers took advantage.

Still, the game came down to the final play when kicker John Love, kicking from the right hash, pushed it left and Pitt celebrated.

With the loss, the Hokies fall to 4-1 and 1-1 in the ACC. Here are six takeaways from Friday's heartbreaking loss.

We'll talk about officiating. It's horrendous. But if Virginia Tech doesn't turn the ball over four times, this game is not even close. Let's focus on three turnovers because one shouldn't have been a turnover. Overall, the Hokies turned the ball over in their own territory three times. The fourth turnover came on quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer's only really bad throw inside the 5-yard line. While Pitt didn't score off every turnover, each was costly. That final turnover took points off the board for the Hokies. If you lose the turnover battle 4-0, you generally never win. The Hokies are/were the better team, but that doesn't matter when you keep turning the ball over. Ultimately, this is why Virginia Tech lost.

Yes, Grunkemeyer passed for 434 yards and three touchdowns, so this was, at least statistically, his best game. He did have three turnovers, but you can only call one his fault. The strip sack was because the right tackle was badly beaten, and the defender made a good play. Pitt had the best defense Grunkemeyer has faced all year. He was dealing. Grunkemeyer made more big-time throws in this game than he had in the previous four games combined. Concerns lingered about his deep ball. He answered those tonight. He dropped a couple in the bucket for Que'Sean Brown. And his dart to Luke Reynolds on fourth down on that final drive was impressive. Grunkemeyer made multiple NFL-level throws on Friday night. Turnovers were not an issue for Grunkemeyer before Friday. I don't suspect they will be a big deal moving forward. He takes care of the ball. The Hokies got a good one in Grunk.

Yes, Pitt scored 35 points, but VT's defense only allowed 299 yards. Pitt had only 191 passing yards between both quarterbacks, and the Hokies held the Panthers to an average of 3.4 yards per carry. The offense kept putting Pry's defense in a bad position all night. For the most part, that unit responded. Trust me, things could've been much worse without some defensive stops. The defense has some issues. The front four doesn't win consistently. Aycen Stevens had another sack, but that was the only one. The Hokies have some disruptive pass rushers, but they need to win more. I still have some concerns about the secondary. Their tackling is bad, and they have too many open receivers every game. Overall, I like the front seven. The linebackers are terrific tacklers. But when you take everything into account, the defense actually kept giving the offense more opportunities, especially in the final quarter. I noticed a lot of Pry hate, but I feel it was unfair. The offense, despite putting up close to 500 yards, made too many mistakes in this one.

One area I will criticize Pry is that he seems slow to adjust. That can hurt you in these closer games. When Pitt lost quarterback Mason Heintschel in the third quarter, it was clear the Panthers would run the ball. They ran it like six straight times for 50 yards and a touchdown. Poor tackling was also an issue here. We saw Pry take a while to adjust to Boston College's quarterback running all over them late last week.

Once the Hokies crossed midfield and kept their timeouts, it was clear they were running the clock down and getting in position to kick a potential game-winning field goal. Why not play for the touchdown? Pitt's defense played better in the second half, but when the Hokies wanted to move the ball through the air, they had no problems. I would have liked to have seen VT keep it going with shorter, safe throws to Luke Reynolds and Que'Sean Brown. Keep the chains moving and maybe take a shot.

For Franklin, I believe it came down to two things. First, he trusted John Love. He should. One of the top kickers in school history, Love has had a terrific career and is considered one of the best kickers in college football. A 36-yarder should've been a chip shot for Love. But he yanked it wide. I can appreciate Franklin trusting his guy here.

Secondly, Franklin just watched his offense turn it over four times. He wasn't going to take another chance with the game on the line. For this reason alone, I get why he played for the field goal.

Let's set aside the Boston College game for a moment because of the weather. In Virginia Tech's other four games, we've seen a familiar theme: the Hokies start fast and build a double-digit lead. Then, in the second half, the offense becomes stale or predictable. A lack of running game plays a part in that. Jeffrey Overton is phenomenal, but the run blocking is lacking. In this game, the Hokies scored 24 in the first and nine in the second half — all in the fourth quarter. We know turnovers played a part in this one, but offensive coordinator Ty Howle must figure out why it is becoming a theme. Is it his playcalling? Is it execution? Howle and Franklin need to figure out the cause and find a way to change it. You can't blow a 14-point lead at home. The Hokies must find a balance between fast starts and sluggish second halves.

Several calls should raise red flags, but we'll focus on a couple. There was an offensive pass interference called on wide receiver Ayden Greene in the first half, where the defender was falling down. Greene caught the ball. It was wiped out. A terrible call.

Now, to the main event. The interception. Just before halftime, Grunkemeyer's pass to Fatrat Brown looked complete. But the officials ruled it an interception, even though it was clear Brown and Cameron Lindsey both had the football. The old rule is that simultaneous possession favors the offense. However, officials ruled it an interception on the field, so replay officials didn't feel there was enough to overturn it. What are we doing here? Check out what NFL rules expert Terry McAuley said about the play. McAuley took it a step further: this wasn't even a simultaneous catch.

McAuley was an NFL official for 20 years and has been NBC's rules analyst for eight years. He is not a Virginia Tech or Pitt fan. This gave Pitt the ball deep in VT territory with around one minute remaining in the first half. After a defensive stand, the Hokies had the ball back with over a minute on the clock, multiple timeouts and a 10-point lead. This error changed everything.

Why do we even have replay if you can't fix the bad calls on the field?

Finally, there's that Love kick. That's a kick he should make 10 out of 10 times. He wanted it on the right hash, and that's where Grunkemeyer got it for him. And he still pushed it wide. That's on him. If you hit it down the middle, we aren't even talking about it.

You had several fans of other teams and national analysts saying they believed it was good. It sure looked like it.

But it should've never come down to this. Let us know what you think.

articles.title: Week 7 takeaways and top performers from high school football
articles.summary: Moeller and Highlands had statement victories while unbeaten teams also had a banner night on Oct. 2.
articles.body:
High school football across Greater Cincinnati is creeping towards the postseason. With just three games remaining for most teams, Week 7 saw the playoff picture grow clearer as conference races were decided and teams made history on the field.

The Greater Catholic League-South crowned a champion in a thriller between Moeller and Elder at Dayton's Welcome Stadium. A Northern Kentucky program elevated itself as a bona fide title contender, while other programs remained undefeated for the first time in decades.

Here are the top things we learned from Week 7 high school football across Greater Cincinnati.

Moeller wins GCL-South title with impressive offense, clutch defense in 35-28 win over Elder

For most of their rivalry showdown with Elder, the only people stopping the Moeller offense was the Crusaders themselves.

The offense needed one more drive to win a title, though, and got it as running back Juice Glover-Brown broke free up the middle for a 26-yard touchdown with 50 seconds left. That gave Moeller a 35-28 win over Elder at Welcome Stadium, and gave the Crusaders the Greater Catholic League-South title for the fourth time in five years. Both teams left Dayton with 5-2 records.

"This win means everything to me and my guys," said senior offensive lineman Kal-El Johnson, a Georgia Tech commit. "We worked hard, man. We had this circle on our calendar since we lost to them (last year). This means so much to me. I love my brothers and we did what we had to do."

Glover-Brown rushed for three touchdowns and had several runs of 20 or more yards, totaling 205 yards on 28 carries. Phil Bailey also had multiple big runs for the Crusaders and had 109 yards total on nine tries. Hunter McLaughlin threw TD passes to Jayden Davis and Dean Schnitzler and threw for 192 yards in the game as Moeller gained 544 yards to 406 for the Panthers.

"Juice, I'm so happy for Juice," Johnson said. "He ran crazy. And don't forget all the other skilled players. Everybody did amazing today, especially Hunter."

Moeller had a fast start, leading 14-0 and limiting Elder to two first downs on its first two drives. Moeller led 21-13 at the half with five drives, three for touchdowns. On one, the Crusaders had a third-and-one and couldn't convert, and missed a short field goal. At the end of the half, Moeller had a touchdown pass waved off by a penalty, and didn't score on the next play to end the half, up 21-13.

After a slow start, Elder senior Kaden Estep threw long TD passes to Jason Forte and Chase Walpole. A long pass to Andrew Lyman set up a Walpole TD catch. Estep led a game-tying drive with three minutes to go, directing the Panthers 81 yards for a TD run, and throwing a two-point pass to Andrew Tallen to tie the game at 28.

That put pressure on the Moeller offense to deliver.

"That situation's a little unique because you feel the urgency to go score. But at the same time, they have three timeouts," Moeller head coach Bert Bathiany said. "If you mess around and leave time on the clock, you could go score and then give it up to them. So it was the balancing act of being efficient on offense, still being able to run the football, completing the ball, and then let that clock roll and just try to get down the field to have a chance for it. We probably scored too fast, honestly."

Bathiany praised the running game and McLaughlin's ability to find other receivers as the Panthers blanketed star receiver Reggie Watson, who had three catches for 43 yards.

"Juice, Phil Bailey, and then how about Tristan Jackson coming back off of injury?" Bathiany said. "Our tight end lead blocking. Jackson Meerdink battling through injuries to go block and our offensive line doing an awesome job. Our receivers, I'm really proud of them. Reggie Watson usually gets the ball a lot, but he drew a lot of attention his way."

Moeller had a rough start with losses to Princeton and Louisville Trinity in the first three games. But the Crusaders have won four straight and are squarely in the mix for the Division I, Region 4 title in what should be a wild and competitive tournament.

"After those two losses, we just came together," Johnson said. "We fixed what we had to fix, we're all set. We're going for state."

Estep completed 21-of-27 passes for 367 yards and three touchdowns. Moeller sacked him four times at key moments. Lyman had 10 catches for 129 yards.

"I don't think anyone does it better than Coach (Doug) Ramsey on the offensive side and just getting the ball to their good players and having explosive plays," Bathiany said. "All their guys are really, really good. So that was the main point is like we had to establish the run and keep the ball away from them. It's a GCL game. They're good. X is good. That's how it always is, right? It doesn't matter what your records are, doesn't matter what happened last week. It's just a battle between these two teams. What's crazy is that team has had two losses in a row and they're one of the best teams in the state. They're gonna be a handful in the playoffs."

Highlands makes another statement in road win over Covington Catholic

Highlands' record might show one loss, but you can make the case the Bluebirds are one of the hottest teams in Kentucky.

Highlands' lone blemish this fall was a season-opening loss on the road to Frederick Douglass, the No. 2 team in Class 6A behind Louisville Trinity.

Since then, Highlands, the top-ranked team in Class 4A has won six straight by an average of 36.3 points per game. In Friday's Skyline Chili Crosstown Showdown in Park Hills, Highlands dominated from the jump in a 38-20 win over Covington Catholic.

The Bluebirds grabbed momentum on the opening snap when senior Gabe Williams made a diving interception by the home sideline. It set up Bryce Armstrong's first rushing touchdown and Highlands never looked back. Williams made another momentous play to open the second half, breaking several tackles on a 41-yard touchdown run that put Highlands up three scores.

Armstrong would unofficially complete 7 of 11 passes while running for 102 yards and two touchdowns. Elsewhere, junior Colt Kremer had a highlight-reel 21-yard touchdown run to put Highlands up 14-0. He also broke a 36-yard touchdown in the final minute of the third quarter to put Highlands up, 38-7, and was named the Skyline Chili Crosstown Showdown MVP.

Kremer had several defensive contributions, including a fourth-down sack. The Bluebirds forced two turnovers and turned the Colonels over on downs twice. Tayden Lorenzen, who had 51 scrimmage yards on 10 touches, had two sacks and senior Cooper Benke recovered a redzone fumble.

"It's a statement win," Williams said. "Beating Boyle (County), 41-21, beating the (Covington Catholic) Colonels at their stadium. This is a great feeling."

Highlands will look to make it seven in a row when they host Elder in Week 8.

CCPA, Dayton, Deer Park historic starts headlines undefeated teams

For the first time in school history, the Dayton Greendevils are 6-0. Having previously matched their best-ever start at 5-0, last achieved in 2020, a dominant 43-12 win against Iroquois has the Greendevils in unchartered waters. Dayton entered the statewide rankings (No. 9 in 1A) for the first time this past week, and could climb even higher after the big win.

Deer Park is having a historic run as well, 7-0 for the first time since the 1981 squad went 10-0. The Wildcats started slowly against Mariemont, leading 3-0 at halftime, but relied on staunch defense for a 17-0 shutout win. The way the schedule works out, Deer Park has a good chance to pick up another win next week before its toughest tests against Indian Hill and Wyoming.

Cincinnati College Preparatory is 7-0 for the first time in school history. The Lions survived Dayton Christian 26-21, continuing an already record-setting year. CCPA had never gone 5-0 in a season before.

Goshen has its first 7-0 start since at least 2004 thanks to a 48-7 win against New Richmond. The Warriors offense has been dominant in each win, scoring no fewer than 34 points in a game. It's Goshen's best run since 2007, when the team rebounded from an opening loss to go 8-0 in conference play.

Elsewhere in Cincinnati, Princeton christened its brand-new stadium with a 47-0 shutout of Mason to improve to 7-0. Sticking in the Cincinnati Hills League, Wyoming improved to 7-0 with a 41-7 win over Madeira. North College Hill proved it's legit with a 43-3 win against Summit Country Day to remain perfect, now 6-0 for the first time since 2010. Hughes cruised past Taft, 38-6, for its first 7-0 start in five years.

Also undefeated in Kentucky is Beechwood, which is 6-0 after blowing out Walton-Verona 63-7. The Tigers only close game came in a 42-35 win against Covington Catholic; otherwise, Beechwood has outscored its opponents 250-10.

Bryce Armstrong, Highlands : Armstrong unofficially ran for 102 yards, threw for 75 more and scored two touchdowns as Highlands rolled to a 38-20 road win over Covington Catholic.

Kaden Estep, Elder : He threw for 367 yards and three touchdowns in the team's 35-28 loss to Moeller.

Anquan Evans, Oak Hills: The senior had his second-straight 150-yard rushing game, gaining 159 yards and three touchdowns on 19 attempts.

Roman Garr, Colerain: Garr was 26-of-44 passing for 352 yards, five touchdowns and an interception in a 41-23 win at Sycamore.

Juice Glover-Brown, Moeller : He rushed for 205 yards and three touchdowns in the Crusaders' 35-28 win over Elder.

Karmelo Jordan, Lakota West: In a 25-0 win at Middletown, he had five receptions for 135 yards and a 67-yard touchdown.

Nile Knutson, Lakota East: The Thunderhawks nearly mounted a 20-point comeback in a 35-31 loss at Fairfield as Knutson threw for 443 yards and three touchdowns.

Colt Kremer, Highlands: The junior was named the Skyline Chili Crosstown Showdown MVP after running for 71 yards and two touchdowns in Highlands' 38-20 win over Covington Catholic.

Brady Lawhon, Harrison: He led Harrison to a 49-13 win against Mount Healthy, going 12-of-16 in the air for 306 yards and four touchdowns.

Ben Markarian, Harrison: He caught just two passes in the 49-13 win against Mount Healthy, but both went for scores of 95 and 43 yards.

Lorenzo McMullen, Jr., Princeton: He hauled in 10 catches for 148 yards and three touchdowns in a 47-0 win over Mason.

Ryan Minges, East Central: He set a new career-best with six rushing touchdowns in a 70-27 win over Connersville. He also eclipsed 3,000 rushing yards in his career.

Tayt Moore, Hamilton: Despite a 42-14 loss to Oak Hills, Moore had seven receptions for 186 yards and a touchdown. He also had a rushing score.

Kenyon Norman, Lakota West: Norman now has 1,181 rushing yards and 20 touchdowns this season after gaining 145 yards and four scores in a 35-0 win over Middletown.

Logan Schmenk, Lebanon: The senior had his third 200-yard rushing game in the 39-29 win over Milford. He had 30 rushes for 256 yards and two scores.

Lincoln Schreiber, Oak Hills: The senior quarterback was 21-for-22 with 330 yards and three touchdowns in a 42-14 win at Hamilton.

Oliver Young, Kings: In a 20-19 loss to Little Miami, Young ran 26 times for 234 yards and a touchdown.

articles.summary: The Turkish destroyer may have just secured a shot at the vacant heavyweight crown.
articles.body:
Shamil Erdogan certified his status as the most dangerous man in ONE Championship's heavyweight MMA division.

The Turkish contender was dominant in the main event of ONE Fight Night 48 , which aired live in U.S. primetime from Bangkok's Lumpinee Stadium on Friday, October 2.

Erdogan ultimately submitted Paul Elliott via rear-naked choke at the 2:28 mark of the second round to extend his perfect record to 14-0 and state his case for a crack at the division's vacant gold.

With a shot at the vacant ONE Heavyweight MMA World Title on the line as a potential reward, the undefeated Turkish destroyer faced the one man capable of matching his finishing instincts – a British titan who earned every one of his wins by stoppage and recently tied ONE Championship's record for the fastest KO in history .

Erdogan, who was a member of both Russia and Turkey's national wrestling teams, wasted no time asserting his will in the opening round. He took the fight to the canvas and spent the better part of five minutes grinding the Englishman down.

He barely let Elliott breathe, rag-dolling him around the ring and wearing him down with punches as the British powerhouse gasped for air and fought to escape the clutches of the Turkish wrecking ball.

Elliott cracked Erdogan early in round two with a right hand that shook the 36-year-old veteran. The Turk tried to engage on the feet, but he paid the price as the Brit spun into a kick.

Second-guessing his chances in the striking exchanges, Erdogan dragged his 34-year-old rival back to the canvas, secured mount, and hammered elbows down. Elliott shimmied this way and that way, but the undefeated star shifted to side control and continued to land damaging elbows and knees.

The Middlesbrough native then gave up his back, and Erdogan kept mauling. When the Brit attempted to get to his feet, he exposed his neck, and the Turkish heavyweight took full advantage of the opening. He slid his arm under the neck, secured the rear-naked choke, and Elliott tapped within seconds.

The submission was another masterclass from one of combat sports' most complete heavyweights. That victory moved his spotless record to a pristine 14-0, bumped his finishing rate to 71 percent, and earned him a US$50,000 performance bonus.

With 14 consecutive wins and no man yet able to solve him, Erdogan has made the strongest possible case for a shot at heavyweight gold.
